```{r setup, include=FALSE}
  "Burundi" = "BDI",
  "Democratic Republic of the Congo" = "COD",
  "Ethiopia" = "ETH",
  "Kenya" = "KEN",
  "Malawi" = "MWI",
  "Rwanda" = "RWA",
  "South Sudan" = "SSD",
  "Uganda" = "UGA",
  "United Republic of Tanzania" = "TZA",
  "Zambia" = "ZMB"
)

fmt_eu_coord <- function (x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(x), 2L), nsmall = 2L, trim = TRUE)
  gsub("\\.", ",", s)
}

interp_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- vals[ord]
  if (yr_num < yrs[1] || yr_num > yrs[length(yrs)]) return(NA_real_)
  idx <- which(yrs == yr_num)
  if (length(idx) > 0L) return(vals[idx[1]])
  stats::approx(x = yrs, y = vals, xout = yr_num, method = "linear")$y
}

fmt_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr_num)
  if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}

fmt_site_peak <- function (e) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return("-")
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  i_pk <- which.max(vals)
  paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(vals[i_pk]), " (", yrs[i_pk], "AD)")
}

  "uganda_protectorate",
  "kenya_colony_highlands_nyanza",
  "kenya_coast_northern_frontier",
  "tanganyika_north_lake",
  "tanganyika_central_coastal",

entry_sub_ids <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
  s <- subregion_lookup[[e$key]]
  if (is.null(s)) "tanganyika_central_coastal" else s
}, character(1))

zone_entries <- setNames(lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- all_entries[entry_sub_ids == sid]
  pks <- vapply(sub, function (e) max(as.numeric(unlist(e$population))), numeric(1))
  sub[order(-pks, vapply(sub, function (e) e$name, character(1)))]
}), subregion_order)

build_gazetteer_df <- function (sub_list) {
  rows <- lapply(sub_list, function (e) {
    iso_code <- iso3_map[[as.character(e$country)]]
    if (is.null(iso_code)) iso_code <- toupper(substr(as.character(e$country), 1L, 3L))
    loc_str <- paste0(iso_code, ": ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]]))
    scope_lbl <- if (identical(as.character(e$population_scope), "metro")) "Metro" else "City"
    data.frame(
      Settlement = as.character(e$name),
      Scope = scope_lbl,
      Location = loc_str,
      `1900AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1900),
      `1910AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1910),
      `1930AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1930),
      `1940AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1940),
      `1950AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1950),
      `1960AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1960),
      Peak = fmt_site_peak(e),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(df) <- NULL
  df
}

n_excluded <- as.integer(summary_cache$wave_saturation_stats$ledger_excluded)
n_candidates <- length(all_entries) + n_excluded
bench_nums <- c(1880, 1900, 1910, 1930, 1940, 1950, 1960)
bench_keys <- as.character(bench_nums)
n_active <- setNames(
  vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, yr)), logical(1))), integer(1)),
  bench_keys
)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates, spatial scopes and multi-period population series for `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed towns, railway depots, *bomas* and coastal ports across ten modern jurisdictions in Colonial East Africa between 1880AD and 1960AD. Screened from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidate colonial records (`r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate aliases merged), the ledger spans eight colonial sub-regions across Uganda, Kenya, Tanganyika, Zanzibar and Ruanda-Urundi together with contiguous borderland posts. Active interpolated entries rise from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1880"]], 0L)` early pre-partition hubs in 1880AD to `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1900"]], 0L)` in 1900AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1910"]], 0L)` in 1910AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1930"]], 0L)` in 1930AD and `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1940"]], 0L)` in 1940AD before narrowing to `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1960"]], 0L)` late-colonial municipal and metropolitan series in 1960AD, led by Nairobi (315k), Mombasa (161,3k agglomeration), Dar es Salaam (159,5k agglomeration), Kampala (158k) and Zanzibar (60,8k).

# Background

Between 1880AD and 1963AD, East Africa's urban network shifted away from nineteenth-century dhow ports and royal courts toward railway junctions, highland settler capitals and colonial district *bomas* [@Gilbert1970CoastalEast; @Johnston1902TheUganda; @Issa2023FromStinkibar]. Early enumerations in Uganda Blue Books, Colonial Office reports and German East African annual surveys captured major ports and administrative stations, while the 1948AD synchronised East African census and Belgian Ruanda-Urundi reports extended uniform headcounts across secondary market towns [@EastAfrica1948Census; @Martin1961EastAfrica; @Office1938ReportHis]. Compiling these dispersed municipal and agglomeration records into a single gazetteer preserves direct traceability between urban trajectories and colonial provincial totals [@Kuczynski1949DemographicSurvey2].

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Sub-Regional Partition

Candidate towns were screened from colonial census tables, Africapolis urban delimitations, East African Institute of Social Research monographs and coastal archaeological inventories [@EastAfrica1948Census; @NMK2021KenyaSites; @Office1933AnnualReport]. Of `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidate entries inside and immediately adjacent to the `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$total_area_km2, 0L)` km² study perimeter bounded over geoBoundaries outlines [@Runfola2020GeoBoundaries], `r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate Wave-3 alias records were merged, retaining `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements across `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` observations (174 strictly interior matches and 7 contiguous cross-border stations assigned to their nearest East African sub-region).

## Spatial Scope and Benchmark Interpolation

To preserve municipal continuity without double-counting peri-urban hinterlands, `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$city_proper, 0L)` city-proper series are catalogued alongside `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$metro, 0L)` metropolitan agglomerations (Nairobi, Mombasa, Dar es Salaam, Kampala, Bujumbura and Kigali) [@Salum2026ReclaimingDarajani]. Tables 1 to 8 report linearly interpolated populations at six chronological checkpoints (1900AD, 1910AD, 1930AD, 1940AD, 1950AD and 1960AD) alongside each entry's observed peak and peak year, marking periods before first enumeration or outside the colonial span with a hyphen (-).

# Testing and Validation

Across all `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` settlements, upper-half Zipf rank-size regression (`r paste0("n=", summary_cache$rank_size$n_fit)`) yields $q = 1,18$ ($R^2 = 0,98$) and full-sample regression yields $q = 1,18$ ($R^2 = 0,99$), aligning closely with the 174 spatially interior peaks plotted in Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank} ($q = 1,06$, $R^2 = 0,99$). Cross-checking against official 1948AD, 1959AD and 1962AD census tables confirms consistent ordering across colonial capitals, port towns and provincial headquarters [@EastAfrica1948Census; @Martin1961EastAfrica].

```{r fig3-ranksize, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig_03_rank_size.png",
  "Zipf rank-size curve across 174 spatially interior settlements (q = 1,06, R² = 0,99) and mean sub-regional density in 1963AD.",
  "fig:settlements-rank",
  arg3_options = list(max_height = "0.38\\textheight")
)
```

# Results

## Uganda Protectorate

Table \ref{tab:sub-uganda} records `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zone_entries[["uganda_protectorate"]]), 0L)` individually assessed settlements across Uganda Protectorate and adjacent northern Congo and southern Sudan border stations, led by Kampala (158k city-proper; 134,8k agglomeration), pre-colonial Kibuga (34k in 1885AD), Jinja (33,6k), Mbale (13,6k in 1960AD) and Entebbe (7,9k in 1948AD) [@Johnston1902TheUganda; @UgandaBlueBook1923; @Amone2018ContestedCitizenship].

```{r tab-uganda, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zone_entries[["uganda_protectorate"]]),
  "Individually assessed settlements in Uganda Protectorate and contiguous northern borderlands (1900AD to 1960AD).",
```

# Limitations

Three caveats govern this settlement ledger. First, 6 of the 181 settlements hold single-date observations (notably pre-colonial courts such as Kibuga and Bweranyange), so interpolated checkpoint columns display a hyphen outside their recorded span. Second, active entries decline from 159 in 1940AD to 30 in 1960AD because colonial district *bomas* enumerated in 1948AD transition into post-colonial national census ledgers beginning after 1960AD [@Martin1961EastAfrica]. Third, separate city-proper and metropolitan agglomeration rows are provided for the six largest capitals and ports to preserve compatibility with both municipal censuses and mid-century Africapolis built-up footprints.

# Conclusion

Taken together, these `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements document the transformation of East African urbanism from nineteenth-century clove, caravan and lacustrine courts to twentieth-century railway capitals, mining hubs and colonial provincial towns across ten jurisdictions between 1880AD and 1960AD.

# Appendix

## Sub-Regional Gazetteer Summary

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-summary} sums the individually assessed site counts and combined interpolated urban populations across all eight colonial sub-regions from 1880AD to 1960AD.

```{r tab-appendix-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(subregion_order, function (sid) {
  sub <- zone_entries[[sid]]
  sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
    vals <- vapply(sub, function (e) {
      p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
      if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
    }, numeric(1))
    viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
  }, character(1)), bench_keys)
  data.frame(
    `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0(sub_by_id[[sid]]$name, " (", viscount_fmt_number(length(sub), 0L), ")"),
    `1880AD` = sums[["1880"]],
    `1900AD` = sums[["1900"]],
    `1910AD` = sums[["1910"]],
    `1930AD` = sums[["1930"]],
    `1940AD` = sums[["1940"]],
    `1950AD` = sums[["1950"]],
    `1960AD` = sums[["1960"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
tot_sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
  vals <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
    p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
    if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
  }, numeric(1))
  viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
}, character(1)), bench_keys)
tot_row <- data.frame(
  `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0("All Subregions (", viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L), ")"),
  `1880AD` = tot_sums[["1880"]],
  `1900AD` = tot_sums[["1900"]],
  `1910AD` = tot_sums[["1910"]],
  `1930AD` = tot_sums[["1930"]],
  `1940AD` = tot_sums[["1940"]],
  `1950AD` = tot_sums[["1950"]],
  `1960AD` = tot_sums[["1960"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(do.call(rbind, sum_rows), tot_row)
rownames(df_sum) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Individually assessed site counts and combined interpolated urban populations across eight colonial sub-regions from 1880AD to 1960AD.",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:gazetteer-summary")
)
```

# Footnotes

Linear interpolation is bounded strictly between each settlement's earliest and latest observed dates; pre-foundation and post-transition benchmarks are left blank with a hyphen (-). For Mombasa, Tanga and Dar es Salaam, city-proper municipal returns and late-colonial Africapolis urban-cluster series are catalogued separately.
